Grade exercise code, working around two gradethis bugs

Source: R/grade_this_code.R
grade_this_code.Rd

A drop-in replacement for gradethis::grade_this_code(), used by the tutorials in this package. It changes two things before the code comparison:

Usage

grade_this_code(...)

Arguments

...

Arguments passed on to gradethis::grade_this_code(), such as correct.

Value

A grading function, like the one returned by gradethis::grade_this_code().

Details

  • color arguments. gradethis 0.2.14 rejects a correct answer when an argument named color (or containing color, such as outlier.color) appears in a different order than in the solution. Its name check sees the student's color, while the solution has already been renamed to colour, the spelling ggplot2 uses internally. This function renames color to colour in argument names of both the student's code and the solutions, so the order no longer matters.

  • Trailing commas. Code such as labs(title = "A", ) makes gradethis crash and report a grading problem. This function marks such code wrong instead, with a message asking the student to remove the trailing comma. [ and [[ calls are left alone, because df[1, ] is not a trailing comma.

  • magrittr pipes. gradethis 0.2.14 mistakes the string "." for the magrittr placeholder when it rewrites %>%, so a correct answer such as df %>% separate_wider_delim(x, delim = ".", ...) is rejected. This function rewrites lhs %>% f(...) as f(lhs, ...) (or puts lhs in place of a bare . argument) before comparing, the same way R's parser already handles |>. Students who use %>% are graded the same as students who use |>.

Only the copies of the code used for grading are changed. The student's code still runs exactly as typed.

Tutorials use it by adding this line to their setup chunk, after gradethis_setup(), so that every grade_this_code() call in their check chunks uses this version:

grade_this_code <- r4dsTutorialsNU::grade_this_code
